# S231 phase-three census: BOTH continuation tables' use on the FITTED build,
# taken so the one-ply shares stand beside S222's 96.62 / 95.15 / 19.15 % and
# S024's 97.56 / 96.19 / 27.14 %, and so the two-ply table's own three shares
# exist at all. A same-tree control at phase one's incumbent vector is beside
# it, so a moved share is attributed to the fit or to the tree rather than
# explained.
#
# WHAT THIS IS. `adocs/data/S024_census_run.py run <engine>` over the same 400
# positions of `adocs/data/S024_census_positions.txt` -- one per game from
# `adocs/data/S219_aa_calibration.pgn`, `random.Random(24)` shuffle, each
# game's own midpoint ply -- at depth 10, Hash 16, `ucinewgame` between
# positions, driven through one persistent UCI process. The script is the one
# S231 phase one extended to eight counters; only the binary under it is new.
#
# THE BINARY. S231's fitted `src/search_params.hpp` -- this project's own SPSA
# lane of 2026-09-19/20, `adocs/data/S231_spsa_trajectory.tsv` -- with the
# eight throwaway counters patched in. Built in a detached worktree at
# `abe251b` with the fitted header copied in; `cmake
# -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release`, its own `build/`, the real tree's never
# touched, the worktree removed after the run. The instrumentation is not in
# the shipping engine and never was: an `info string cont_hist_census` line is
# not on the UCI surface `tests/test_uci_surface.cpp` guards. The exact diff is
# at the bottom of this file, so the run reproduces without it ever having been
# in the tree. The script writes `adocs/data/S024_census.tsv`, so it was run
# from the worktree's copy and S024's own artefact in this tree was never
# touched -- what S222 did.
#
# THE CONTROL. The same instrumented binary rebuilt with `abe251b`'s own
# `src/search_params.hpp` -- phase one's incumbent 17/18/26 twice -- and the
# same 400 positions re-run. It separates the vector from the tree, and here
# it says the fit moved almost nothing: the tree is 2.2 % smaller (29450590
# nodes against 30121175) and every share is within four tenths of a point of
# the control's. The one-ply non-zero share is 19.89 % fitted against 20.22 %
# at the incumbent vector, so the fitted vector reads a non-zero one-ply entry
# slightly **less** often, by 0.34 points; the two-ply non-zero share is
# 27.51 % against 27.31 %, 0.20 points the other way. Both runs were repeated
# once and reproduced to the counter.
#
# THE READING. The two-ply table is **not** inert wiring: the move two plies
# back exists at 94.24 % of quiet cutoffs and the term is consulted on 95.72 %
# of quiet `score_move()` evaluations -- within a point and a half of the
# one-ply table's 96.53 % and 95.30 % -- and **27.51 % of those consultations
# read a non-zero entry, against the one-ply table's 19.89 % on the same
# run**. The two-ply table is the one that more often has something to say,
# which is a fact about this tree's shape and not a claim about strength: what
# a table returns is not what it is worth (DEC-019), and
# `adocs/data/S231_sprt.sh` decides the step. The one-ply figures are S222's
# own profile again, a third of a point apart on all three, on a tree 3.4 %
# smaller than S222's 30474552.
#
# WHAT THE THREE NEW DENOMINATORS ARE, since they differ from the one-ply
# three's by more than the guard: `writes_with_prev2` is over
# `writes_total` and `reads_with_prev2` over `reads_total`, so the two-ply
# write share is 2.3 points under the one-ply one -- ply 0, ply 1 and the node
# two plies after a null move pass no two-ply key, where only ply 0 and the
# node after a pass are missing a one-ply one.
#
# SUMMARY, FITTED VECTOR (18/17/24 one-ply, 18/20/24 two-ply), as the script
# printed it:
#
#   positions: 400
#   total nodes: 29450590
#   wall time: 9.7 s
